purpose: Benchmark entry: a real, public, historical DeFi exploit used to measure whether Argus's detection classes catch its on-chain footprint. Adapt the referenced DeFiHackLabs PoC + fork-validate to upgrade SPEC -> CONFIRMED.
mechanism: Beanstalk on-chain governance used the native Stalk token for voting power, measured via a non-flash-loan-resistant in-block snapshot. The attacker first submitted malicious proposal BIP-18 (an InitDiamondCut-style facet that would transfer all protocol assets to the attacker), then in a later transaction took roughly 1B USD in flash loans (DAI/USDC/USDT from Aave, BEAN from Uniswap V2, LUSD from SushiSwap), deposited them into Beanstalk to mint a greater-than-two-thirds supermajority of Stalk voting power within a single transaction. With supermajority reached, the attacker called the Beanstalk Diamond emergencyCommit() function, which bypassed the normal proposal lifecycle (only a 24h proposal age required) and executed the malicious BIP via delegatecall. The delegatecall ran attacker-controlled logic that swept the protocol BEAN3CRV and BEANLUSD collateral to the attacker contract. The flash loans were repaid in the same transaction; the attacker also pushed BIP-19 to donate 250k USD of BEAN to Ukraine. Net theft of non-BEAN collateral was converted to roughly 24,830 WETH (approx 76M USD).

provenance.loss_usd_approx: approx 182M USD total protocol loss; approx 76M USD (24,830 WETH) net attacker profit
provenance.note: attacker_address is the SENDER of attack_tx_hash; attack_block is that tx's block (Etherscan-verifiable).
